verdict.rationale: Notion's first-party developer docs say connections can subscribe to real-time events (page updates, property changes, new comments) via webhooks, and that Notion sends a secure HTTP POST to your webhook endpoint when a page or database changes. That is a registrable outbound HTTP callback a programmatic consumer can receive. Missing for 10: detail on how endpoints are registered and verified, signature and retry/delivery semantics, a full event catalog, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: Connections can subscribe to real-time events — like page updates, property changes, and new comments — via webhooks.
Whenever a page or database changes, Notion sends a secure HTTP POST request to your webhook endpoint.
